thread:
emily: FYI customer on Dedicated is seeing intermittent 5xx when calling our hosted API over PrivateLink. They get TLS handshake timeouts / connection reset from the ENI. logs + repro below.

raj: Which VPCE id and are they hitting api.redwood.run or a custom domain?

emily: vpce-0a1b2c3d in account 123456789012, subnets a/b. They resolve api.redwood.run to the vpce private DNS -> 10.0.1.23. curl shows: 'curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' after ClientHello. Tried from an EC2 in same subnet, same result.

leah: Can they paste openssl s_client output and a tcpdump? Cert fingerprint/SNI will narrow it.

mike: Also check their SG/NACL egress. I've seen strict egress allowlists block OCSP/CRL endpoints and that causes handshakes to stall. Also watch ephemeral port return rules.

emily: s_client they sent:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect vpce-0a1b2c3d-abcdef.vpce-svc.amazonaws.com:443 -servername api.redwood.run -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
140... handshake failure
---
no peer certificate available
---
EOF
```
Packet capture: ClientHello -> ServerHello not seen, then RST from remote ENI.

raj: RST from ENI could mean backend refused TCP because Host/SNI didn't match expected. With PrivateLink the DNS resolves to endpoint IP but the TLS SNI must be the original hostname (api.redwood.run). If their proxy rewrites SNI/Host to the vpce FQDN we will reject. Did their proxy change Host header or SNI?

emily: They admitted their outbound proxy rewrites host headers to the resolved A record (vpce FQDN) for logging. They didn't set explicit SNI. Repro: curl directly to vpce FQDN fails; curl --resolve 'api.redwood.run:443:10.0.1.23' https://api.redwood.run/ returns 200.

leah: That confirms SNI/Host mismatch. Two notes: 1) ensure client SNI is api.redwood.run, not vpce hostname; 2) check egress allowlist for OCSP/DNS since certificate validation can require contacting CA.

infra-bot: Service check: api.redwood.run: OK. vpce-0a1b2c3d status: Available. No infra deploys in last 6h.

mike: Ask them to run these quick checks and paste outputs:
1) openssl s_client -connect <vpce-dns>:443 -servername api.redwood.run -tlsextdebug
2) curl -v --resolve 'api.redwood.run:443:<vpce-ip>' https://api.redwood.run/
3) tcpdump -nni any 'tcp port 443' and show the ClientHello SNI
Also confirm SG allows ephemeral reply ports (1024-65535) / return traffic and NACL not blocking ephemeral ranges.

emily: They ran the --resolve test and it worked (200). They changed proxy to preserve original Host header/SNI and opened outbound to ocsp.digicert.com. After that the curl from their clients succeeded.

raj: Root cause: customer-side proxy was rewriting SNI/Host to the endpoint hostname + strict egress allowlist blocked OCSP, causing handshake to fail/reset.

leah: I'll add this case to the PrivateLink troubleshooting playbook with: openssl repro commands, signs to look for (ClientHello SNI mismatch, RST from ENI), and firewall checklist (allow OCSP + CA issuer + ephemeral ports).

mike: I'll write a short KB for support: 'PrivateLink TLS failures: SNI/Host rewrite + OCSP egress' with the exact commands. :thumbsup:

emily: Customer rolled a canary config preserving Host/SNI and allowed OCSP outbound; 24h observation planned before closing.

leah: Adding tag: root_cause: "client-proxy-sni-rewrite + egress-block-ocsp" and will close after confirm.

emily: thanks everyone — will follow up with customer status update. :raised_hands:
